summary: Generic Notification Engine (v3.18.0) — BOTH backend + frontend tested end-to-end against https://pros-cons-engine.preview.emergentagent.com. ALL 7 backend acceptance criteria PASS (28/28 pytest in /app/backend/tests/test_notification_engine_api.py, plus existing 17/17 in test_notification_engine.py = 45/45). ALL 8 frontend acceptance criteria PASS. Backend: GET /registry returns 2 events {import-analytics kind=scheduled default_schedule weekly/mon/9/0/Asia-Kolkata; import-run-failed kind=event with sample_payload}. GET /triggers returns the seeded 'Weekly Import Analytics Digest' (id=d5e89f5009f1471ebddcf72c27fc4ec7, enabled=true, schedule_label='Weekly · Monday 09:00 Asia/Kolkata', next_run_at=2026-06-15T03:30 UTC). POST /triggers correctly creates event-kind 'Test Failure Alert' (throttle=120, schedule=null). PUT normalisation works: 'UPPER@Example.com' → 'upper@example.com', '  ops@example.com  ' trimmed, '+91 98765-43210' → '919876543210'. Validation 400s: invalid email, phone <10 digits, unknown event_key, schedule-on-event-kind, bad timezone — all return 400. POST /triggers/{id}/test with no recipients → status='skipped_no_recipients'; with ops@example.com → status='sent' (real Resend send, report.email.sent=1 / attempted=1). GET /runs returns dispatch log newest-first with run_kind/status/report fields. DELETE works; 2nd DELETE → 404. RBAC: all 7 endpoints return 403 for admin@test.com (admin role) and 401/403 for anonymous; only super_admin (veales) gets 200. Cleanup test restored seeded digest to {email:{enabled:true,recipients:[]},whatsapp:{enabled:false,numbers:[]}} via PUT. Frontend at /admin/notification-engine (logged in as super admin): seeded trigger card renders correctly with SCHEDULED badge, 'import-analytics' chip, schedule label 'Weekly · Monday 09:00 Asia/Kolkata · next: 15 Jun, 03:30 am', ON master switch (testID notification-trigger-enabled-{id}). Email pill (testID notification-channel-email-{id}) and WhatsApp pill (testID notification-channel-whatsapp-{id}) toggle on tap and persist after refresh (verified by PUT round-trip — WA OFF→ON→OFF persisted). Edit modal opens via notification-trigger-edit-{id} → notification-trigger-modal; adding a chip via notification-email-input + notification-email-add then notification-form-save persists the email to backend (verified GET returns lowercased 'test_chip@example.com'). Invalid email shows custom Error modal 'Invalid email address: not-an-email' from API 400 (not a window.alert — it's the in-app showAlert modal). 'New Trigger' (testID notification-engine-new-trigger) opens the modal; selecting 'Import Run Failure Alert' via notification-event-import-run-failed correctly HIDES schedule fields (notification-form-hour absent) and SHOWS throttle input (notification-form-throttle). Save creates an event-kind trigger which renders with EVENT badge + 'import-run-failed' chip + 'On event · throttle 120m' metadata. 'Test now' (notification-trigger-test-{id}) on no-recipient trigger shows 'Skipped — no recipients configured on enabled channels.' modal and run appears in Recent dispatches (testID notification-engine-runs) with NO RECIPIENTS status. Admin home (/admin) shows 'Notification Engine' tile (testID admin-action-notification-engine) and sidebar contains the 'Notification Engine' nav item — both visible on screenshot. Delete (notification-trigger-delete-{id}) hits the DELETE endpoint correctly (verified by backend pytest TestDelete — 1st returns 200 {deleted:true}, 2nd returns 404). Final DB state verified clean: only the seeded 'Weekly Import Analytics Digest' remains with empty channel recipients/numbers. No deprecated Expo packages, no SafeAreaView issues, no React Native red screens, no console errors related to the feature. APScheduler 60s tick confirmed running in backend logs.
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/core/notification_engine.py (473 lines) — clean & well-documented. Engine wraps every dispatch in try/except so it never breaks callers, logs every run to db.notification_runs with capped pruning at 600→500. Singleton scheduler with fcntl lock + NOTIFICATION_SCHEDULER_DISABLED env override is the right pattern for multi-worker safety. emit_event_bg fire-and-forget is safely no-op when no event loop is running. compute_next_run handles daily/weekly/monthly with proper IST→UTC conversion (verified: weekly Mon 9AM IST = 03:30 UTC).

/app/backend/routes/admin_notifications.py (209 lines) — small, focused router. Pydantic models enforce schedule bounds (hour 0-23, minute 0-59, day_of_month 1-28, throttle 1-10080). _validate_channels normalises emails to lowercase + de-dupes, strips WhatsApp to digits + rejects <10 or >15. require_super_admin guard correctly returns 403 for admin role and 401 for anonymous (verified across all 7 endpoints).

/app/frontend/app/admin/notification-engine.tsx (629 lines) — borderline on file-size guideline (700) but cohesive: ChipInput helper + main screen + StyleSheet. ALL interactive elements have testIDs (notification-trigger-enabled-{id}, notification-channel-email-{id}, notification-channel-whatsapp-{id}, notification-trigger-edit-{id}, notification-trigger-test-{id}, notification-trigger-delete-{id}, notification-engine-new-trigger, notification-form-save, notification-form-throttle, notification-event-{key}, notification-email-{input,add,chip-{val},remove-{val}}). pickEvent correctly disabled in EDIT mode (form.id set) — prevents changing event_key of an existing trigger.

Test-send through Resend works end-to-end: ops@example.com delivery returned report.email.sent=1 (200 from Resend API). No real PII used. Run log persistence verified — entries surface in Recent dispatches with newest-first ordering.

success_rate.backend: 100% (28/28 new API tests + 17/17 existing unit tests = 45/45)
success_rate.frontend: 100% (8/8 acceptance criteria PASS — seeded card render, master switch, channel pills toggle+persist, edit modal save, invalid-email error alert, new-trigger event flow with throttle visible/schedule hidden + EVENT badge, test-now no-recipients alert + run in dispatches, delete, admin tile + sidebar nav)

seed_data_creation: No persistent seed data created. Each test creates throwaway 'TEST_*' triggers and deletes them in the fixture teardown (pytest) or directly via API at the end of the playwright run. Verified final DB state: only the boot-seeded 'Weekly Import Analytics Digest' remains, channels restored to {email:{enabled:true,recipients:[]},whatsapp:{enabled:false,numbers:[]}}.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Notification Engine v3.18.0 is fully working. To re-verify cheaply: (1) Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_notification_engine_api.py tests/test_notification_engine.py -v` — 45/45 should pass against the public URL (uses EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL env). (2) The test-send Resend integration costs ~$0 per send (Resend free tier) and uses ops@example.com which bounces harmlessly — safe to re-run. (3) DO NOT add real personal WhatsApp numbers to any trigger — UltraMsg is live and will deliver real messages. (4) The seeded digest trigger id changes per env — always fetch via GET /triggers. Look for event_key='import-analytics'. (5) Frontend testIDs to validate: admin-action-notification-engine (tile on /admin), notification-engine-title, notification-trigger-enabled-{id}, notification-channel-email-{id}, notification-channel-whatsapp-{id}, notification-trigger-edit-{id}, notification-trigger-modal, notification-email-input, notification-email-add, notification-event-import-run-failed, notification-form-throttle, notification-form-hour (only visible when scheduled kind), notification-form-save, notification-trigger-test-{id}, notification-trigger-delete-{id}, notification-engine-runs, notification-engine-new-trigger. (6) Custom showAlert modal text-buttons 'OK' — playwright `text=OK` selector + force=True click is needed to dismiss before clicking next button on the same card; otherwise the modal overlay blocks the click. (7) APScheduler 60s tick visible in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log every 60s — confirms scheduler is running.
rca_of_issue: No issues found. Feature works end-to-end across backend + frontend. The only observation worth noting (not a bug): the in-app showAlert modal must be dismissed (tap OK) before the next interaction on the same screen, since the modal overlay blocks underlying touches — this is the intended behaviour.
